Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 series in September this autumn as usual, but this year's launch will reflect the special circumstances of the iPhone release during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic in several ways.

How this autumn's iPhone launch will differ from Apple's usual practice

Apple has many highly successful products, but the iPhone has always been its flagship, accounting for a large share of the company's overall revenue.

Therefore, it is hardly surprising that Apple strives to maintain consistency in its iPhone launches. By keeping to a predictable new iPhone release schedule, Apple can better satisfy Wall Street and its customers.

Typically, Apple unveils the new iPhone — usually four new models — in early September, with all models shipping in late September.

But 2020 was an exceptional year due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

That year's autumn iPhone lineup was not announced until October, with only two new models shipping initially and the remaining two not arriving until November.

There are rumours this year that we may see some similar disruptions to Apple's launch schedule.

Although an September launch event is still widely expected, Apple may not ship all new iPhone models at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models are likely to be available for purchase initially: the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The much-anticipated foldable model, the iPhone Ultra, is expected to be unveiled in September, but rumours suggest its release date may be slightly delayed, potentially arriving several weeks after the Pro models.

Apple may also differ from its usual practice in terms of the total number of new iPhone models.

If rumours that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 will be postponed until spring 2027 are true, then only three new models will debut this autumn — the smallest autumn iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether due to strategic considerations, challenges posed by the global memory crisis, or the difficulties of mass-producing a brand-new foldable device, Apple's autumn 2026 launch could well echo several scenarios from 2020.

What new offerings would you like to see Apple bring to this autumn's iPhone launch? Let us know in the comments.
